title: Shelve a tall paperback into a 40 mm gap in a packed shelf without disturbing the row
instruction: Put the loose red paperback upright into the gap in the row on the shelf, spine out and square, with its spine level with the other spines. Leave every other book upright and where it is, and take both hands off.
context: Almost everyone has squeezed a book back into a full shelf: the gap is only a few millimetres wider than the book, so it has to be brought in square, slid in until its spine is level with its neighbours' spines, and let go without tipping the row. A book pushed in crooked catches a neighbour and tips the row; one left proud or turned is mis-shelved and jams the next. A ten-second clip shows the whole job: pick up the book, slide it in, take the hands away, row still standing.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +305 mm and -305 mm. The top shelf of a small open bookcase stands on the table in front of the left arm; nothing is above it. Fixed: a shelf board 135.5 x 191 x 12 mm (melamine chipboard, white) at x 235 to 370.5 mm, y 209.5 to 400.5 mm; two side panels 147.5 x 18 x 240 mm (pine) at x 235 to 382.5 mm, y 191.5 to 209.5 mm and 400.5 to 418.5 mm; a back panel 12 x 191 x 240 mm (pine) at x 370.5 to 382.5 mm. Six upright paperbacks A to F (card cover, paper pages; each 105 mm along x, 25 mm thick, 148 mm tall, 0.16 kg), spines toward the robot at x 265 mm, backs at x 370 mm, stand on the shelf from panel to panel: A at y 210 to 235, B 235 to 260, C 260 to 285 mm, then a gap 285 to 325 mm (40 mm wide, centre y 305 mm), then D 325 to 350, E 350 to 375, F 375 to 400 mm. The end books touch the side panels. The new book is a red paperback, 105 mm along x, 30 mm thick, 185 mm tall, 0.26 kg, standing upright on the table (the book truck's top) at x 117.5 to 222.5 mm, y 420 to 450 mm, spine toward the robot: it is 5 mm clear of each neighbour once centred in the gap. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer reads all seven books and both grippers every step and keeps each book's largest tilt (its height axis from vertical). Underside = the centre of a book's bottom face. Spine line = mean x of the bottom edges of C's and D's spines. Gap line = midway between C's and D's undersides. Clear = distance from a neighbour's face to the new book's bottom corners. Score 0 if at any moment a neighbour tilts over 45 degrees, or the new book does while not held (no gripper's finger zone within 10 mm of it with its pads under 75 mm apart; a book tilted in the hand is fine if it is seated and upright at the end), or the new book's lowest point is more than 10 mm below the table top (dropped off the table), if a neighbour ends off the shelf, or if hands are not off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from every book and no book's centre moves over 5 mm or turns over 5 degrees from where it was at the start of that second (motion you can see on video). Row upright: each of A to F tilted under 5 degrees at the end, never over 20, and within 6 mm of its place. Seated: new book's underside within 3 mm of the shelf top, its centre within 3 mm of the gap line, every bottom corner 2 mm or more clear of C and of D, tilt under 3 degrees, turned under 3 degrees from spine-out, its spine within 5 mm of the spine line. In the gap: all four bottom corners between C and D, underside within 3 mm of the shelf, tilt under 10 degrees, turned under 15, spine within 40 mm of the line. Score 1.0 seated and row upright; 0.5 in the gap and row upright; 0.25 in the gap with the row disturbed (each of A to F under 20 degrees at the end and within 20 mm of its place); else 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held a further 1 s. Real trial: feeler gauges or a rule for clearances, a try square for tilt (3 degrees is 9.7 mm lean over 185 mm), a straightedge across the spines, a pencil outline of each book's place, 30 mm spacer blocks and a video of the last second (nothing visibly moving, judged against a 5 mm pencil mark or the shelf edge).
reset_notes: Stand A to F upright from panel to panel with the 40 mm gap between C and D and the end books touching the panels; check each against its pencilled outline. Stand the new book at x 117.5 to 222.5 mm, y 420 to 450 mm, spine toward the robot. Replace any book with a warped cover or a loosened spine.
fidelity: Rigid boxes: no flexing covers, page block or rounded spine; the bookcase is fixed boxes. Friction is the simulator's default (static 1.2, dynamic 1.0), grippier than real covers (about 0.4); at 0.4 the 0.26 kg book needs only about 3.2 N squeeze per pad, well within the gripper. The spine is not drawn, so the scorer checks the book's heading. The new book is taller and thicker than its neighbours so the grippers can hold its top above them.
